evidence.adapted_model_is_less_perturbable: The clearest new fact: on the adapted backbone, selected and random produce byte-identical completions on 6/12 prompts and prompt 10 is identical across all six conditions. The adapted (rationale-SFT'd) model answers in stable templated form and is LESS responsive to the injected prefix than either the raw-1.7B or the 0.6B champion. So adaptation did not make memory surface; it made the model harder to perturb.
evidence.not_a_selector_artifact: Per #230 the selector is exonerated at 1024, and the adapted-2048 oracle/soft (the strongest query-conditioned objects) are still generic here, so the failure is not selection.
evidence.sanity: 0 reserved-ID emissions, 0 NaN, 0 empty completions in all six conditions.

conclusion: On the ADAPTED Qwen3-1.7B backbone (outputs/merged-model-distill-v2-rationale-1.7b, ladder 0.8667 vs base 0.7286) the corrected post-transform object, deployed through the validated inputs_embeds surface with the #232 Phase-4-trained projection, is STILL generic -- 0/72 persona markers, exactly as at 1024 (#228/#230), raw-2048 (#231), and 0.6B. This was the last untested variable in the #232 chain: with the selector already exonerated (#230), and width ruled out (#231), this probe rules out this specific adaptation recipe too. The three named hypotheses for the mechanism's generic generation are now exhausted: selector, width, and backbone adaptation. What remains is either corpus/persona thinness (#196) or a reconsideration of whether frozen-backbone soft-prompt injection is the right mechanism at all.
recommended_next_step: State plainly: #230 (selector), #231 (width), and #232 (this adaptation recipe) are all ruled out for generation legibility. The two remaining paths are (a) corpus/persona specificity -- #196, testing whether the persona memory text is rich enough to be discriminable at all, and (b) reconsidering the injection mechanism itself. Do NOT pick one for the project owner; do NOT re-open the selector or retrain this backbone; do NOT run CQ4. The choice between (a) and (b) is the project owner's call.
recall_generation_divergence: #232 Phase 4 found the recall proxies got WORSE on the adapted encoder (val 0.1562, 3.8x chance; probe 0.0521, 2.5x chance) than on the raw-1.7B encoder (0.2761/0.1823), while the same adaptation RAISED the ladder +13.8pp. Phase 5 now shows generation is generic regardless. Together: ladder quality, recall proxies, and generation legibility are three different axes, and recall@1 remains not a valid proxy for legibility in this mechanism -- now demonstrated across two backbones, two adaptation states, and two widths.
